question: In Newland's law of octaves, the first element is ______ and the last known element is ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogen, thorium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newland's law of octaves was proposed by **John Newlands**, an English chemist, in **1864**.
 
• The law states that when elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic weights, every eighth element exhibits similar properties to the first one, akin to musical octaves.
 
• In Newland's arrangement, **hydrogen** was placed as the first element.
 
• The last known element in Newland's table was **thorium**, as only 56 elements were known at the time.
 
• Although Newland's law of octaves was a significant step in developing the periodic table, it was criticized for its limitations in accommodating newly discovered elements and anomalies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table Evolution**

 
 
• Newland's law of octaves was one of the first systematic attempts to classify elements.
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev later improved the periodic classification by arranging elements based on atomic weights and predicted properties of undiscovered elements.
 
• Henry Moseley further refined the table by introducing atomic numbers as the basis for arrangement, which is the modern periodic law.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Newland's Law**
 
 
• The law could not accommodate elements discovered after thorium.
 
• It failed to explain the properties of elements beyond calcium (20th element).
 
• Grouping dissimilar elements like cobalt and nickel with halogens was a significant drawback.
 
 
 
• **Thorium**
 
 
• Thorium is a radioactive actinide metal with the atomic number 90.
 
• It was among the last elements known during Newland's time.
 
• Thorium is used in nuclear reactors and has applications in high-temperature ceramics.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen**
 
 
• Hydrogen is the first element in the periodic table with an atomic number of 1.
 
• It is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe.
 
• Hydrogen is essential in forming water and serves as a key fuel source in energy production.
